formation.title: The Boar-Banner Rises
formation.text:
From the granite ridges above the Tungabhadra, the imperial gopurams of Vijayanagara lift their tiered crowns over a city of half a million. The throne of Hampi is yours: the Karnata Rajya restored, dharma defended, the southern peoples gathered under the saffron Varaha. But your court must choose its character. The Saluva-Tuluva transition has shown that the empire can be governed in two voices, and the rituals you privilege will define what your dynasty becomes.

Will you raise the empire as the great patron of Saiva temple and Brahmin learning, anchoring legitimacy in the goddess Pampa-Virupaksha and the Sringeri matha, or will you walk the path of Krishnadeva Raya: a cosmopolitan court of Telugu poets, Vaishnava devotion, Portuguese horse-traders, and Persian envoys, an empire whose dharma flows outward through commerce?

This choice unlocks a destiny path in the Traditions tab.

options.text: The Pampa-Virupaksha Line: temple, tank, and Brahmin sanction

modifiers.name: The Pampa-Virupaksha Line
modifiers.text: The empire is anchored in Saiva temple-ritual and the Sringeri matha. Brahmin sanction and monumental temple-building convert the southern peoples and raise vast manpower for the imperial host.

options.text: The Tuluva Court: Telugu verse, Vaishnava devotion, foreign trade

modifiers.name: The Tuluva Court
modifiers.text: Vaishnava devotion, Telugu literary patronage, and the cosmopolitan court of Krishnadeva Raya. The Karnata empire trades with Portuguese, Persian, and Arab merchants and welcomes envoys from across the Indian Ocean.

advances.name: Sangama Foundation
advances.text: Harihara and Bukka, captives of the Tughluqs turned founders, raise Vijayanagara on the southern bank of the Tungabhadra in 1336 as a Hindu bulwark against the Sultanate's southern advance. The dynasty takes its legitimacy from the Saiva matha at Sringeri and the goddess Pampa of Hampi.

advances.name: Kuravar Levies
advances.text: The hill-peoples of the Western and Eastern Ghats (Kuravas, Irulas, and the broader forest castes) provide skirmishing archers and javelin-bearers to the imperial host. They know the jungle and the hill-track; the imperial cavalry rides through territory they have already mapped.

advances.name: Tank Irrigation
advances.text: The Tungabhadra valley is laced with kere: earthen tanks fed by anicut diversion-dams across the river. The Hiriya canal alone irrigates Hampi, Kamalapura, and the imperial estates. Karnata agriculture is feast where the rains alone would be famine.

advances.name: Dravidian Temple Architecture
advances.text: Pyramidal gopurams, tiered mantapas, sculpted yali-pillars, monolithic Nandis, processional streets aligned to the sanctum: the Vijayanagara school synthesizes the Chola, Pallava, Hoysala, and Pandya inheritances into a unified imperial idiom.

advances.name: The Amara-Nayaka System
advances.text: Territorial governorships called amarams are granted to nayaka commanders in exchange for sworn military service: cavalry, infantry, elephants, forts, and a remitted share of revenue. The empire raises armies through a feudal-military bureaucracy unique to the Karnata.

event.title: The Amara-Nayaka System Codified
event.text:
Across the empire, the imperial court formalizes the system of amaram tenure: territorial governorships granted to nayaka commanders in exchange for sworn military service. Each amara-nayaka maintains a quota of cavalry, infantry, elephants, and forts; collects revenue from his territory's peasants, craftsmen, and merchants; and remits a portion to the imperial treasury. The system promises a vast standing army at the dynasty's call. It also creates dozens of military lords with armies of their own.

The court must decide how tightly the imperial chains will bind them.

options.text: Audit them strictly: tax registers, sealed quotas, rotating postings

modifiers.name: Audited Nayakas
modifiers.text: The amara-nayakas serve under sealed registers and rotating postings. The crown holds them on a tight tether, and the imperial treasury fills.

options.text: Reward them generously: levies in exchange for autonomy

modifiers.name: Imperial Nayaka Levy
modifiers.text: The amara-nayakas raise vast levies in exchange for free hand in their amarams. The empire's banners fly thicker than ever, though the grandees grow.

advances.name: Swarnakara Bronze Guilds
advances.text: The swarnakara (the goldsmiths of the south) continue the Chola lost-wax tradition that produced the Nataraja and the Tirupati bronzes. Imperial workshops pour bronze processional icons, ritual lamps, sword-fittings, and elephant-armor for the empire's temples and armies.

advances.name: The Court of Devaraya II
advances.text: Devaraya II, called Gajabetegara (the elephant-hunter), receives at Hampi the embassy of Abdul Razzaq from Timurid Herat (1442) and the merchant Niccolo de' Conti from Venice. The court's diplomatic reach now spans Persia, the Bahmani Deccan, the Indian Ocean, and the Mediterranean.

advances.name: Imperial Elephant Corps
advances.text: The empire keeps thousands of war elephants in the stables of Hampi, Penukonda, and Anegondi. Armored howdahs, palanquin commanders, and a mahout caste of hereditary elephant-handlers sustain the gajapati tradition the Karnata empire wears as its own.

advances.name: The Coronation of Krishnadeva Raya
advances.text: The third son of Tuluva Narasa Nayaka, born 1471, is crowned at Hampi in 1509. Krishnadeva, soldier, scholar, statesman, polyglot, poet of the Amuktamalyada, will reign for twenty years and bring the empire to its absolute zenith.

event.title: The Coronation of Krishnadeva Raya
event.text:
The third son of Tuluva Narasa Nayaka has taken the throne at Hampi. Krishnadeva (chess-master, polyglot, poet of the Amuktamalyada and patron of Allasani Peddana, scholar-warrior, and the most magnetic ruler in southern memory) is crowned at an enlarged Virupaksha temple in 1509. His reign offers two faces: Krishnadeva the philosopher-king who composed Telugu verses on statecraft, or Krishnadeva the dig-vijaya conqueror who broke the Gajapati at Kondavidu and humbled Bijapur at Raichur.

How shall your court remember him?

options.text: As scholar-emperor: convene the Bhuvana Vijaya

modifiers.name: The Amuktamalyada Reign
modifiers.text: The emperor's verse and patronage flower across Telugu, Sanskrit, Tamil, and Kannada. The court is the lodestar of Dravidian letters.

options.text: As dig-vijaya conqueror: ride against the doab

modifiers.name: Dig-Vijaya Campaign
modifiers.text: The Karnata armies sweep across the Krishna-Tungabhadra doab and crash through the Gajapati frontier. The empire's prestige spreads with its banners.

advances.name: The Ashtadiggajas
advances.text: Eight 'elephants of the directions' fill the imperial Bhuvana Vijaya (the Hall of World-Conquest). Allasani Peddana, Nandi Thimmana, Tenali Ramakrishna, Pingali Surana, and their fellows raise Telugu literature to a golden age and make Hampi the Athens of the south.

event.title: The Hall of World-Conquest
event.text:
Within the new pillared hall called Bhuvana Vijaya (the Hall of World-Conquest), the emperor convenes the literary court. Two factions wait on his patronage. The Ashtadiggajas, the eight 'elephants of the directions,' speak in Telugu: Allasani Peddana the andhra-kavita-pitamaha, Nandi Thimmana of Parijatapaharanam, Pingali Surana of the bilingual Raghava-Pandaviyam, Tenali Ramakrishna the wit. Beside them stand the Sanskrit kavya pandits of Vyasa Tirtha's circle, scholars of the Madhva matha and the dvaita Vedanta, keepers of pan-Indian classical learning, advocates of a Sanskrit court legible to every brahmin from Kashmir to Sri Lanka.

The emperor's purse can elevate one school to court office. The other will keep its honour but lose its first claim on imperial patronage.

options.text: Telugu is now a language of dharma. The Ashtadiggajas in residence.

modifiers.name: Telugu Bhuvana
modifiers.text: The Ashtadiggajas in residence at the Hall of World-Conquest. Vernacular Telugu becomes the language of empire: administered, taught, and recited in courts from Pulicat to the Krishna. The literary energy of a continent flows through Karnata channels.

options.text: Vyasa Tirtha at our right hand. Sanskrit kavya is the empire's voice.

modifiers.name: Sanskrit Kavya
modifiers.text: Vyasa Tirtha's dvaita matha rises at court. Pan-Indian classical scholarship sets the tone of imperial discourse: every brahmin north and south recognizes the Karnata as an emperor of dharma, and the empire's chronicles are read in the same Sanskrit from Kashmir to Lanka.

advances.name: The Goa Horse Trade
advances.text: The Portuguese capture of Goa in 1510 reroutes the Arabian and Persian horse-trade through Karnata-allied factors. The empire's heavy cavalry, long hampered by the southern climate, finally rides on imported Arabians at scale.

event.title: Horses from the Sea
event.text:
The southern climate breaks horses; the empire imports its cavalry mounts. The Portuguese capture of Goa in 1510 has rearranged the trade. Arabian and Persian war-horses, once the lifeblood of the Bahmani cavalry, can now flow through Goa under continuous Portuguese factorage: reliable, sealed, and dependent on the Estado da India's goodwill. Or the empire can deal directly with the Hormuzi and Mappilla merchant houses at Bhatkal and Honnavar, paying lower prices for shipments that arrive when they arrive, with the Persian Gulf factors taking their margin in spices and saltpetre rather than Portuguese silver.

The Konkan ports are at the empire's command. The choice is whose horse-merchants they will host.

options.text: The Portuguese factor at Goa. Continuous supply, by treaty.

modifiers.name: Goa Partnership
modifiers.text: Portuguese factors at Goa deliver Arabian and Persian war-horses to the imperial cavalry on continuous contract. The supply is reliable, the cavalry is mounted, and the Portuguese are courted with imperial favour.

options.text: The Hormuzi houses at Bhatkal. The horses come, and so does no foreign garrison.

modifiers.name: Hormuzi Merchants
modifiers.text: Hormuzi and Mappilla merchant houses bring Persian and Arabian horses directly to Bhatkal and Honnavar. The cavalry is mounted at lower price and without Portuguese leverage, but the Hindu court must learn to accommodate Konkani Muslim merchant princes, and the brahmins of the imperial assembly grumble.

advances.name: Chola Bronzework Tradition
advances.text: The Chola lost-wax tradition that produced the Nataraja and the Tirupati bronzes is preserved in the imperial swarnakara workshops. Processional icons, royal jewelry, and ritual lamps now flow from Karnata workshops to courts and temples across the Indian Ocean.

advances.name: The Gajadhwaja Elephant Corps
advances.text: Under the gajadhwaja (the elephant-banner), the imperial corps of war elephants is reorganized into permanent regiments. Howdahs are armored against firearms; mahouts are trained from childhood; the Karnata gajasena becomes the most feared elephant force in the subcontinent.

advances.name: The Lessons of Talikota
advances.text: Whether averted or survived, the lessons of the Talikota plain are absorbed: never a divided command; never trust mercenary captains beyond their last paid month; always reserve a regrouping force; always know the enemy's pre-battle envoys.

event.title: The Shadow of Talikota Averted
event.text:
The four-power Sultanate coalition assembled north of the Krishna in the manner of 1565: Bijapur, Ahmadnagar, Golconda, Bidar uniting their cavalry against the Karnata empire. In our world, on that Friday at Talikota, the Gilani brothers commanding Rama Raya's Muslim regiments defected mid-battle and the imperial line collapsed. The empire's regent was beheaded; Hampi was sacked for five months and never recovered.

In this age, your court has read that history before it could happen. The court purges, drills, and reorganizes the host. Two reform paths beckon: a unified command structure under a single field-marshal, or a thorough purification of court factions and dynastic rivals.

options.text: Establish unified field command and Frankish-style drill

modifiers.name: Unified Imperial Command
modifiers.text: The imperial host fights as one column under a single Senapati, drilled in continental fashion with massed artillery. The disasters of divided command are not repeated.

options.text: Purge the factions; no Gilanis at our throat again

modifiers.name: Purified Court
modifiers.text: Court factions are dissolved, foreign commanders examined for loyalty, and the temple establishment reaffirmed at the heart of imperial ritual. The empire stands ideologically unified.

advances.name: Telugu as Imperial Court Language
advances.text: Krishnadeva's Amuktamalyada legacy elevates Telugu beside Sanskrit and Kannada as a language of imperial administration. Inscriptions, grants, and court epics now run in four scripts; the Dravidian peoples are bound through their own letters into the imperial vision.

advances.name: The Aravidu Restoration
advances.text: The Aravidu dynasty under Tirumala and his successors restores the empire from the southern capitals (Penukonda, Chandragiri, Vellore) and recovers the doab. The Karnata Rajya endures where in our timeline it fell.

advances.name: The Reincorporation of the Nayaka Kingdoms
advances.text: Madurai under the Nayaks of Madurai, Thanjavur under the Nayaks of Thanjavur, Gingee, Mysore, Ikkeri: the breakaway nayaka principalities of the post-Talikota collapse are brought back under direct imperial authority. The Karnata Rajya stands whole.

advances.name: Coromandel Textile Manufactories
advances.text: Madras, Pulicat, Masulipatnam, Pondicherry, Sadras: the Coromandel coast textile manufactories produce the finest painted and dyed cottons in the early-modern world. Karnata cloth dresses Persia, Arabia, the Spice Islands, and increasingly Europe.

advances.name: The Imperial Treasury
advances.text: Karnata fiscal reform consolidates the multiple regional revenue systems into a unified imperial treasury at Hampi, with subsidiary treasuries at Penukonda and Madurai. Revenue assessment is regularized; surplus funds the imperial monumental program.

advances.name: Pulicat Emporia
advances.text: Madras, Pulicat, Masulipatnam, Sadras, Pondicherry: the Coromandel coast emporia handle the empire's spice and textile trade. Imperial factors negotiate with European trading companies on Karnata terms.

advances.name: Imperial Conscription
advances.text: The amara-nayaka levies are reformed under uniform imperial command: standardized regiments, drilled in Frankish fashion, equipped from imperial arsenals, conscripted by lottery from the four-language districts. The Karnata army modernizes without losing its territorial roots.

advances.name: Imperial Cannon Doctrine
advances.text: The swarnakara workshops are reorganized as imperial cannon-foundries, casting bronze and iron field-pieces for the Karnata army. The Dravidian metallurgical tradition turns its skill from temple bell to siege gun.

advances.name: The Dravidian Cabinet
advances.text: Modern cabinet government conducts its business in Telugu, Tamil, Kannada, and Malayalam: the four-language imperial machinery that no European empire ever managed to displace.

advances.name: Modernized Nayaka Garrisons
advances.text: Amara-nayaka troop quotas modernize: firearms in place of swords and bows, drilled musketry, standardized uniforms. The nayaka forts are held by modern garrisons without losing their territorial character.

destiny.name: The Karnata Destiny
destiny.text: Vijayanagara is restored: the imperial gopurams rise above Hampi and the southern peoples gather under the saffron Varaha. But what shall the empire become? Two long-term projects beckon: the great work of dharma in the north, and the great work of the Indian Ocean. Stability above all is required to undertake either.

conditions.text: Stability at least 25

event.title: The Karnata Destiny
event.text: From the Tungabhadra granite, from the throne of Hampi, the empire surveys the work of generations to come. The Saluva, Tuluva, and Aravidu lines have founded a dharma-raj that no Sultanate's coalition can break; the matha pontiffs have blessed the imperial regalia; the swarnakara guilds have cast a Garuda-banner of bronze and gold. Now the long work begins. Two destinies open. One faces north: to reclaim the Deccan plateau and beyond, to undo the conquest of the fourteenth century, to restore the heartland of dharma in the imperial heart of Bharata. One faces seaward: to inherit the Indian Ocean, to plant the imperial banner on Lanka, the Maldives, Malacca, Hormuz, Aden, and to build the trade-empire that no European company can match. The court chooses; the empire commits.

options.text: Let the destiny of Vijayanagara unfold.

destiny.name: March on the Bahmani Frontier
destiny.text: The successor sultanates of the Bahmani (Bidar and Bijapur first among them) sit across the Krishna and the Tungabhadra, the very gates of imperial expansion northward. The Karnata host must reclaim them before the Deccan plateau itself can be called Vijayanagara's.

conditions.text: Karnata Destiny: the Pampa-Virupaksha line.
Own Bidar, or a subject owns it
Own Bijapur, or a subject owns it
Army size at least 30

event.title: The Krishna Crossed
event.text: Bidar's walls have fallen; Bijapur's nobles have surrendered the citadel. The Krishna has been crossed in force, and the imperial banners ride into the open Deccan plateau for the first time since the Tughluq invasions of the fourteenth century. Across the empire, temple bells ring; the Sringeri matha sends gold-leaf manuscripts to Hampi; the amara-nayakas swear new oaths on the dust of the conquered fortresses. The Bahmani frontier (the southern boundary of dharma's eclipse for two centuries) is no more.

options.text: Onward to the Tapti and the Narmada.

destiny.name: Reclaim the Deccan Plateau
destiny.text: Beyond Bidar and Bijapur lie Gulbarga, Daulatabad, and Ahmednagar: the Bahmani heartland and the great Tughluq capital that once tried to swallow the south. To take them is to reverse the southward conquest of the fourteenth century and reset the imperial frontier on the Tapti. Vijayanagara itself must grow into a capital fit for the whole plateau.

conditions.text: Own Gulbarga, or a subject owns it
Own Daulatabad, or a subject owns it
Own Ahmednagar, or a subject owns it
We own Vijayanagar and its development is at least 49

event.title: Daulatabad Restored
event.text: The great fortress of Daulatabad (Devagiri before the Tughluqs renamed it, the rock-citadel that Muhammad bin Tughluq tried to make the capital of his collapsing empire) is in Karnata hands. Gulbarga, the original Bahmani capital, has surrendered. Ahmednagar's nobles fly the Garuda. The Deccan plateau, from the Tapti to the Krishna, is restored to dharma. Two questions face the court: how to disburse the conquered wealth, and how to hold the new frontier.

options.text: Distribute the Sultanate treasures: refill the imperial coffers

modifiers.name: Treasures of the Sultanate
modifiers.text: The looted wealth of Daulatabad and Bidar floods the imperial treasury and the temple endowments. Prosperity rises across the empire; but the legitimacy-cost of plundering ancient cities weighs on the imperial conscience.

options.text: Garrison the Deccan: hold every fort, finance with war loans

modifiers.name: Deccan Garrisoned
modifiers.text: Every Bahmani fort holds a Karnata garrison, financed by imperial war-loans from Hampi's banking houses. The empire's logistical reach extends across the plateau and the casus belli of dharma-restoration carries new weight; the loan-interest is a price worth paying.

destiny.name: The Imperial Heartland Restored
destiny.text: From Surat on the Gujarat coast to Agra in the Yamuna basin, from Golconda's diamond mines to Warangal's ancient citadel: the Karnata empire claims the imperial frontiers of an undivided dharma-raj. The Diwan-Khana of the south rises in Hampi, a chancery worthy of the heir of Bharata.

conditions.text: Own Surat, or a subject owns it
Own Agra, or a subject owns it
Own Golconda, or a subject owns it
Own Warangal, or a subject owns it
Prestige at least 75
Army size at least 75

event.title: The Empire of Bharata
event.text: From Surat on the Gujarati coast (where the Mughal emperor Akbar will not now sit) through Agra and the Yamuna basin, through Golconda's diamond country, to Warangal's old Kakatiya citadel: the imperial frontier has reached the high-water mark of every great south-Indian dynasty before. The Diwan-Khana rises at Hampi, a chancery whose vaulted halls speak Telugu, Sanskrit, Persian, and Marathi. The court must decide what kind of empire to be: an empire of dharma's peace, or the chakravartin's empire of universal sovereignty.

options.text: Dharma Paramount: rule by the imperial peace

modifiers.name: Dharma Paramount
modifiers.text: The empire rules through dharma's peace: tolerant of every Hindu strand and every other strand, ruling by negotiation and example. The court is alive with purpose, and the empire's diplomacy carries the weight of moral authority.

options.text: Chakravartin: claim universal sovereignty over Bharata

modifiers.name: Chakravartin
modifiers.text: The emperor takes the title chakravartin: universal monarch, wheel-turner, sovereign of the four directions. Subjects of every kind serve the imperial wheel; the prestige of the empire's name does not fade; new wars open before it as the wheel turns.

destiny.name: The Konkan Thalassocracy
destiny.text: The Konkan coast (Bombay's harbor, Goa's Portuguese-built quays) is the empire's first ocean. To control it is to set the dharma-banner over the Arabian Sea trade and to receive horse, silver, and ship-timber on the empire's own terms.

conditions.text: Karnata Destiny: the Tuluva court.
Own Thana, or a subject owns it
Own Goa, or a subject owns it
Gold at least 1000

event.title: The Arabian Sea is Ours
event.text: Goa's quays (built by the Portuguese, repaired by Karnata craftsmen) and Bombay's deepwater harbor now fly the Garuda banner. Imperial squadrons of shallow-draft frigates patrol the Konkan coast from Sindhudurg to Bhatkal. Arabian horse, Persian silver, Yemeni coffee, and Aceh pepper now flow through Karnata factors at terms set in Hampi. The empire has become an ocean-power, and the long thalassocracy of the south begins.

options.text: The Arabian Sea is the empire's first lake.

destiny.name: Lanka and the Maldive Atolls
destiny.text: Sri Lanka (Kotte, Kandy) and the long arc of Maldive atolls lie astride the trade lanes from East Africa to Sumatra. To plant the imperial banner there is to take the keys to the Indian Ocean. The treasury must be full enough to fit out the fleets first.

conditions.text: Own Kotte, or a subject owns it
Own Kandy, or a subject owns it
Own Male Atoll, or a subject owns it
Gold at least 2000

event.title: The Pearl of the South
event.text: Kotte's tooth-relic, Kandy's hill-citadel, and the long arc of the Maldive atolls (Male, Addu, Thiladhunmathi) are imperial possessions. The pearl-fisheries of Mannar and the cowrie-currency of the Maldives flow into the imperial economy. The Theravada sangha of Lanka has been honored at Hampi; the Maldive sultans serve as imperial vassals. Two strategies suggest themselves: rule Lanka as a directly-governed imperial province, or knit the atolls into a far-flung trading-factor network.

options.text: Lanka as imperial province: direct rule, monumental rebuilding

modifiers.name: The Lanka Dominion
modifiers.text: Sri Lanka is governed as a directly-administered imperial province. Imperial roads, monumental temple-rebuilding, and devastation-recovery brigades restore the island. The empire's colonial reach extends, and the inflation of conquered specie is checked by orderly administration.

options.text: Maldive trade factories: light-touch network of imperial agents

modifiers.name: The Maldive Factor Network
modifiers.text: Imperial factors are stationed across the Maldive atolls, Lanka's southern ports, and the Laccadive coast. Merchant-establishment costs collapse; merchant capacity grows; imperial squadrons enforce blockades against any rival who dares the southern seas.

destiny.name: Lord of the Indian Ocean
destiny.text: Malacca to the east, Hormuz to the west, Aden at the gate of the Red Sea: the three pivots of the Indian Ocean. To hold them is to be sovereign of the largest trade ocean on earth. Pulicat must grow into a great port, and there the Coromandel Bourse rises to clear the world's silk and spice.

conditions.text: Own Malacca, or a subject owns it
Own Hormuz, or a subject owns it
Own 'Adan, or a subject owns it
Gold at least 3000
We own Pazhaverkadu (Pulicat) and its development is at least 54

event.title: Lord of Three Oceans
event.text: Malacca, Hormuz, Aden: the three pivots of the Indian Ocean trade. Malacca on the strait that separates the Bay of Bengal from the South China Sea; Hormuz on the strait that gates the Persian Gulf; Aden at the bottleneck of the Red Sea. The empire that holds all three is sovereign of the trade-ocean, lord of the silk and spice that flows from Canton to Lisbon. The Coromandel Imperial Bourse rises at Pulicat: the largest customs-house and exchange in the Indian Ocean. The empire stands at its trade-empire zenith.

options.text: The Karnata Pax of the Seas: imperial fleets enforce the order

modifiers.name: The Karnata Pax of the Seas
modifiers.text: The imperial fleet enforces the peace of three oceans. Heavy ships of the line and light frigates together; reinforced hulls; rigorously trained crews. No European company's squadron can match the empire's order of battle in the Indian Ocean.

options.text: Imperial trading companies: chartered factors run the network

modifiers.name: Imperial Trading Companies
modifiers.text: Chartered Karnata trading companies (modeled on the European pattern, but answering to Hampi) run the Indian Ocean factory network. Imperial migration flows outward; exploration expands the network. The army at home grows expensive to reinforce as the best men find their fortunes overseas.

units.name: Kuravar Archers
units.text: Hill-people skirmishers from the Western and Eastern Ghats. Light-armored, mobile, and at home in jungle and hill terrain, the Kuravar archers screen and harry far ahead of the imperial cavalry.

units.name: Imperial Arabian Horse
units.text: Heavy cavalry mounted on Arabian and Persian war horses imported through Goa. The Karnata empire's signature shock arm under the Tuluva and Aravidu dynasties: fast, disciplined, and a counterweight to Sultanate cavalry.

units.name: Gajadhwaja War Elephant
units.text: Permanent regiments of armored elephants under the imperial gajadhwaja banner. Mahouts trained from childhood; howdahs reinforced against firearms; the elephant-banner of the south.

buildings.name: Dravidian Temple Complex
buildings.text: Imperial Saiva-Vaishnava temple complex with monumental gopurams, pillared mantapas, sculpted yali-columns, and a sacred tank. The Hampi style (Vittala, Hazara Rama, Virupaksha) exported across the empire.

buildings.name: Amara-Nayaka Estate
buildings.text: Fortified manorial seat of an amara-nayaka: a military lord holding territory in exchange for cavalry, infantry, elephants, and forts. The backbone of Karnata military organization.

buildings.name: Gajashala
buildings.text: The domed elephant stables of a royal seat, as they stand at Hampi. War elephants are kept, armoured and trained here by a hereditary caste of mahouts, and regiments can be raised where the stables stand. The animals eat a district's worth of grain.

children.text: Elephants is produced in the market

buildings.name: Tungabhadra Anicut
buildings.text: Earthen tank fed by an anicut diversion-dam. The Hiriya canal model: monsoon flows captured into reservoirs, channels feeding paddy, cane and orchard. Built where the land grows rice, sugar cane or fruit, and raises its harvest. The imperial agricultural foundation.

children.text: The location's raw material is Rice
The location's raw material is Sugar
The location's raw material is Fruit

buildings.name: Bhuvana Vijaya
buildings.text: The Hall of World-Conquest. Imperial pillared hall housing the court of poets (the Ashtadiggajas) and the literary academies in Telugu, Sanskrit, Kannada, and Tamil. The Karnata court of letters.

buildings.name: Swarnakara Workshop
buildings.text: Goldsmith and bronze-caster guild workshop continuing the Chola lost-wax tradition. Processional icons, ritual lamps, jewelry, and sword-fittings flow from Karnata workshops across the Indian Ocean.

buildings.name: Pulicat Factory
buildings.text: Karnata coastal trade factory and warehouse complex. Storehouses, customs posts, factor's quarters, and quayside loading docks for the Coromandel cotton, indigo, and spice trade.

buildings.name: Imperial Diwan-Khana
buildings.text: The chancery of a restored empire. Vaulted halls in a Hindu-imperial register that echoes the Tughluq and Bahmani palaces of the north: a deliberate visual claim on the architectural inheritance of the Deccan plateau, now restored to dharma. Every imperial decree affecting Bharata passes through these halls.

buildings.name: Coromandel Imperial Bourse
buildings.text: The grand customs-house and trading exchange of the Karnata Indian Ocean empire. A pillared coastal hall where imperial factors clear silk from Canton, spice from Malacca, horse from Hormuz, coffee from Aden, and Coromandel cotton bound for half the world. The financial heart of the southern thalassocracy.

list.name: Pampa-Virupaksha Devasthanam
list.text: The imperial Saiva temple complex at Hampi, where Virupaksha (a form of Shiva) was installed as tutelary deity of the empire. From Harihara I in 1336, royal grants and edicts were issued in the god's name: the emperor styled himself merely the deity's deputy, and the Pampakshetra ritual centered the Tungabhadra valley as sacred geography. The devasthanam administered temple lands, brahmadeya grants, and the donative economy that bound the Sangama and Tuluva courts to the Saiva clerical establishment.

conditions.text: Owns Vijayanagar

list.name: Diwan-Kacheri
list.text: The imperial chancery and revenue bureau formalized under Krishnadeva Raya (r. 1509-1529) and described in his Telugu political treatise the Amuktamalyada. The Pradhani (chief minister) headed eight ministerial portfolios; the Rayasam corps of royal scribes issued sasanas (copperplate edicts) across the realm in Kannada, Telugu, Tamil, and Sanskrit. The Diwan-Kacheri retained a strong oral-Sanskritic legal tradition alongside Telugu-language administration, distinguishing it from the contemporary Persianate chanceries of the Deccan sultanates.

list.name: Tirumala Devasthanam
list.text: The Vaishnava temple of Venkateswara on the Tirumala hills above Tirupati. Krishnadeva Raya's seven personal visits and lavish endowments (1513-1521) made the shrine the Vaishnava counterpart to the Saiva Pampa-Virupaksha at Hampi, balancing the empire's religious patronage. By the late sixteenth century Tirumala had become the wealthiest temple in early-modern South India through pilgrim hundi cash offerings, grain reserves, and a parallel temple-banking system that lent at favourable rates to merchants and Nayaka aristocrats.

list.name: Coromandel Customs
list.text: The eastern-coast revenue apparatus administering Pulicat, Negapatnam, San Thome (Mylapore), and Masulipatnam. The Vijayanagara state collected sungam (transit duties) through imperially-appointed Adhikari port-governors and licensed the Ayyavole 500 and Manigramam merchant guilds to handle long-distance Indian Ocean trade. Portuguese, Persian, and later Dutch factors paid customs in cash and bullion; Coromandel textiles reached as far as Aceh, Pegu, and the Spice Islands.
